how_to_use: Every package copies this file byte for byte and pins its sha256: hc-dashboard worker/test-vectors/crew-plan-cases.json (master copy once P2 starts), hc-app tests/fixtures/crew-plan-cases.json, hc-field-app scripts/fixtures/crew-plan-cases.json (build 45) and HC Secure Backups/tools/crew/073/tests/crew-plan-cases.json. A copy that differs fails the run.

Each case names the packages that must pass it: sql (the PGlite twin of 073), worker (worker/crew-plan.js pure rules and the scans), hcapp (public/crewplan.js), field (build 45). A package runs every case that lists it.
input.extends names a fixture; fixtures extend fixtures. Resolve by merge_rules below, then apply the case rows, settings, now, worker_mode and remove.
expected asserts only what it lists (match_rules below). A listed field must equal exactly; a field not listed is not checked.
Synthetic data only. Never add a real client, address, email, phone, amount or crew last name. The App Review address is the one real string (070 hard codes it).

packages.sql: run-073-pglite.mjs on the post-072 production shape (072 stubs plus 070 and 073)

app.is: the App Review login (by email), in never_schedule

table_owner.role: the migration owner (bypasses grants, not triggers)
table_owner.is: used only to prove the triggers

merge_rules: A fixture or case input is {extends, now, worker_mode, settings, rows, remove} plus case-only keys (calls, then, refuse_samples, words_from, fault, and the worker or app keys).
Resolve extends first (recursively). now and worker_mode replace. settings merge key by key into crew_plan_settings (id 1).
rows: per table, a row whose key (table_keys) matches an existing row REPLACES it whole; any other row is appended. A key with two parts is written "a|b" in remove.
remove: per table, the listed keys are dropped after rows are applied.

Rows hold only the columns the rules read; every other column takes its table default. route_answers is not a table: it is what computeRoute answered (or what the robot cached), keyed by start site and end (a site id or an address). order_departures rows are reused for a garage start as design 4.2 says.
worker_mode is the CREW_PLAN_MODE secret: null means unset (off). crew_plan_days field approved_tasks_md5 '$md5(tasks)' is computed by the loader after insert.

then: a list of follow-up steps run on the SAME state after the case calls; each step may carry rows, settings, now, worker_mode and calls, and has its own expected entry in expected.then (same order).

Named tasks: anywhere in fixtures or inputs, the string "$task:NAME" is a deep copy of named_tasks.NAME, and an object {"$task": "NAME", field: value, ...} is that copy with those fields replaced. Expand these before anything else. Expected sections never use them.

Table rows omit columns whose value is null (and orders omit deposit_cents 0 and logo_received false): an omitted column takes its table default. Stored tasks inside crew_plan_days are always whole (3.4 shape plus route_at and why).
match_rules: days[]: one entry per (market, day). tasks lists the FULL ordered task list (R13 order) unless tasks_exact is false (then each listed key must exist, order free). Each listed task field must equal; gaps is the exact sorted set of codes; gaps_include and gaps_exclude are subset checks.

days[].gaps: the exact list of day gap entries in the stored order (red first, then task_key with null first, then code); gaps_include is a subset check. A gap entry is {code, level, owner_only, task_key, words}.

no_tasks: those market days have no task (a day row may still exist for gaps). no_task_kinds and no_task_keys apply to every day. never_people: no task anywhere names those crew_people ids. never_sites: no task names that site.
gaps_absent: no gap entry with those codes on any day. forbidden_text_in_words: no stored words value contains any of these strings.

replies[]: one per call in order; a reply object is a subset match of the jsonb reply; {error: "22023"} means the call raised that SQLSTATE (message compared when given); error "any" means any refusal. same_as_reply: n means equal to reply n except repeat.

after: unchanged_days (the whole row is byte-identical), locked_columns_unchanged (tasks, cancelled_keys, approved_version, approved_tasks_md5, approved_at, approved_by and helper_told are byte-identical by md5), push_queue.added (rows added by the calls) and push_queue.rows (subset match of each added row: id, title, body, body.kind as body_kind, tokens, headers collapse_id, aps thread-id, and aps interruption-level time-sensitive as time_sensitive), log_added (crew_plan_log rows added).

Read helpers: day_keys is the ordered list of [market, day] returned; day_checks are subset checks on one returned day; task_* maps are by task key; forbidden_keys may appear at no depth; forbidden_text may appear in no string.

Helper names (all subset checks): day_checks.task_keys (exact ordered keys of that day), gap_codes (exact sorted codes of the returned gaps), task_people_names (people display names in order), task_held, task_hold_reason, task_starts, task_words, task_mine, held_tasks (fields of a held row), proposal_task_starts, proposal (null means none returned); jobs_include (by order_id; extras_billed is the billed flag of each extra in order), people_include (by person_id), sites_count, rules_count; after.days[]: task_keys, task_count, sources, words, cancelled_keys, kept_md5, inputs_md5, proposal_md5, proposal_reasons, proposal_gap_codes, task_starts, approved_by, new_owner_row (the one own: row added); worker: sends (the exact banner list the tick queues, before queue dedupe), never_to, never_kinds_for_market, digest_lines, calls (call counts), robot_put (the put the robot sends for that day), departure (the order_departures row fields written), calls_crew_origins.

formats.supply_window: The first two clock times in coconut_supply_orders.delivery_window ("Arrival 10:00 AM - 06:00 PM" -> 10:00 to 18:00). Fewer than two: no window.

rules.R1: Days: day = 072 hc_order_family_day(coalesce(delivery_at_utc, event_start_at)): a 00:00 UTC marker is that date, any other time is its New York date. Window today - 1 to today + 8 in market time. Only markets with rule planned = 1 are planned (needs an active base with confirmed coordinates). Every job day in another market gets ONE owner-only market_not_planned day gap and no rows.
rules.R2: Jobs: stages invoiced, deposit_paid, paid_full only (leads and fulfilled or complete never). One job day per 072 family day with its OWN coconuts_qty; a child takes its head job card and, if it has no cut, the head cut. A child of a cancelled head, or a cancelled day, has no rows. day_not_linked: no external_invoice_id and no parent_order_id. count_missing: coconuts_qty null. count_disputed: an open or still_on 072 finding count_differs or days_differ on that order. calendar_check: any other open or still_on finding on that order (one entry per code per row). addon_not_on_card: a live, not voided, read add-on on the head whose line name matches /cart/i with no cart extra, /cooler/i with no cooler extra, or /staff|attendant/i with no on_site entries.
rules.R3: Prep: card prep skip = no prep row. auto (and base, staging) ALWAYS make a prep row on the use day; cut = crack_type, else invoice cracking, else the family head cut (review counts as none); no cut = amber cut_unknown. Branding: card yes = branded, no = not; auto = branded when stamp ordered or received, logo_received true or logo_asset set; stamp not_needed = not branded, no gap; else amber branding_unknown.
rules.R4: boxes = ceil(coconuts / 9) per job (null when the count is missing; cars then assume 1). Use day = D - 1 when the job has a prep row, else D.
rules.R5: Supply (049's shared rule): counting rows are status confirmed with a delivery_date (and, in ny, ship_to_garage true) or status claimed. Short test per (market, P = D - 1) over that P's job days: need = ceil(sum of known coconuts / 9) + 1 per job with no count; email credit = drops taken first in, first out (delivery_date, then id) from those landing on or before the group's latest use day, groups in ascending P, until need is met; have = max(email credit, weee claims with prep_day P) + other-supplier claims with prep_day P; short = need - have. boxes_short (red, owner only) goes on every prep and deliver row of the group. Within a group the taken drops are split to jobs in R13 order of their deliver rows, each up to its own boxes (1 when unknown). no_supply_record: day gap on each job day of a planned market that has NO counting row in the window. Claims make no rows; a staged job leaning on a claim gets claim_no_drop_day.
rules.R6: Staging per JOB: staged when the card says always, or auto and any of its drops waits (use day - landing day) more than the base hold_nights. hold_unconfirmed (amber) when the card is auto, an active cold storage exists, a drop waits 1 night or more and the base hold is not confirmed. never with too long a wait: red hold_too_long. Staged but no active cold storage WITH an address: red no_staging and the plan stays at the base. Staged and a drop waits more than the cold storage hold_nights, or hold_nights is null: red hold_unknown. A staged job's drops get ONE move row per drop on the landing day; boxes not moved get a receive row (one per drop).
rules.R7: Prep place: not staged = the base. Staged: card staging = the cold storage; card base = the base, and the move happens AFTER prep on the use day (when any_time), with the R6 hold check at the base; card auto with cold storage can_prep yes = the cold storage; otherwise red prep_place_unknown and from_site null. Never a guessed place.
rules.R8: Times. receive: start, end = the drop window, time_source supply_window. move: start, end = the window, when after_drop. prep: when any_time; amber late_supply when a drop allocated to the job lands on the use day. deliver: arrival = the confirmed delivery_request window, else the invoice delivery_window (amber time_unconfirmed), parsed by parseArrivalTime on the job day; a pending order_time_proposals time that is earlier wins (amber time_proposal_pending); kind assumed = red needs_ampm and no arrival. leave_by = leaveByMs(arrival, drive, ferry) floored to the minute (60 min buffer, 30 min ferry). start = card crew_start (time_source crew_start; amber no_arrival when no arrival; amber start_after_leave_by when crew_start > leave_by - load_minutes), else leave_by - load_minutes (time_source arrival). Drive: for a base start the order_departures drive_seconds for the same order and dest_address first, else the route answer; no route answer yet = amber route_pending and no start; 3 failed runs = red no_time. No arrival and no crew start = red no_time. No address = no route tried. extras: start = the card time at the VENUE (time_source owner); missing time red equipment_no_time; missing home red equipment_no_home. on_site rows from the card. Amber early_start when start < earliest_start_min; amber site_closed when a row starts at a site before opens_at, or a move ends (window end + drive + unload_minutes) after the cold storage closes_at.
rules.R8_busy: Busy windows (busy_from, busy_to) for clash and long_day: deliver = start to arrival + unload_minutes; no arrival = start + drive + unload; no drive either = start + 2 h; no start = none. extras = start - drive (unknown: 60 min) to start + 30 min (pickup: to its end). on_site = start to end. move = window end to window end + drive (unknown: 60 min) + unload; no window = none. receive = the drop window, only when receive_people >= 1. prep = none. Overlap is strict (a.from < b.to and b.from < a.to).
rules.R9: Address: to_address = delivery_notes, else venue (Navigate). Neither = red no_address. address_conflict (red, owner only) when invoice_fulfillment.read_status is complete and its zip differs from the to_address zip. out_of_area (red, day gap, no prep and no deliver row; drops still checked in; the job still counts in R5) when the address names a state outside the market drive area, or the route answer ends more than 250 km from the base (routeSanity too_far).
rules.R10: Cars and people: move and deliver cars = ceil(boxes / boxes_per_car) (1 when boxes unknown); extras 1 car; receive, prep, on_site 0 cars. need = max(cars, 2 when boxes > two_people_over else 1, card people_min, extra people) for move, deliver and extras; receive need = receive_people; prep need 1; on_site need = its people. The first `cars` people drive cars 1..cars in order; the rest ride (car null). rule_unconfirmed (one entry per row) when boxes_per_car, two_people_over (move, deliver) or receive_people (receive) is not confirmed. A missing rule: red rule_missing, 1 car assumed.
rules.R11: Who: pool = active crew_people passing hc_crew_person_ok for the market (roster: worker active, has a login, live field_workers.market = the market, not in never_schedule, not the App Review email; auto_pick yes; helpers: helper_market = the market, auto_pick ask; the owner row is auto_pick no and never auto-picked). Days in date order, rows in R13 order; candidates: the family continuity list first (people already on that job family, in order), then roster by rank, then fewest rows in the same Mon to Sun week (approved days included), then first name, then id; then helpers by rank, name. Approved days off are skipped silently; pending ones stay with amber pending_day_off. Take FREE candidates (no busy overlap that day) until need; if still short take busy candidates in order and flag red clash on this row; if still short red people_short (or red no_crew_in_market when the pool is empty). helper_ask (amber) on every row with a helper. drop_window_overlap (amber) on a receive or move row when receive_people >= 1 and one of its people has a timed row at another place starting inside the window or less than 2 hours before it. Never invents a person.
rules.R12: long_day (amber) when one person's first busy_from to last busy_to that day is MORE than max_span_hours; on that person's first row.
rules.R13: Output per market day: rows sorted by start (no start last), then kind, then key, in byte order; task gaps sorted; day gaps red first, then task_key (null first), then code. inputs_md5 = md5 of the sorted JSON of every fact used for that day (the job days on D and D + 1, the drops landing on D or allocated to those jobs, days off touching D, and the versions of settings, rules, sites, people and job cards). Same inputs give byte-identical output.
rules.held: Held at READ time, never stored: a row whose order (or its family head) is cancelled; a deliver row whose order job day is no longer its plan day (moved) or whose live Navigate address differs from its to_address (address). Fulfilled or complete is done, not held. A count change alone is not held. Non-owners see the held words and no place, time, boxes or cars; the owner sees held and hold_reason.
rules.never: Never: the App Review login or a never_schedule worker on any row (robot, put, save and notice each check), inactive rows, money, client contact, supplier or shortage words in crew text, the word billed, anything sent to a helper, Telegram to crew. With CREW_PLAN_MODE unset everything is off and the departure plan is byte-identical to today (garage origin).

contract_decisions: market_not_planned is a 41st gap code (amber, owner only, day level) for the design's "one owner-only note per job day" in unplanned markets.
Stored gap words never name the supplier (no_supply_record and claim_no_drop_day included); HC App may add supplier words in its own owner UI from the fix text.
Gap placement (gap_codes.placement), rule_unconfirmed as one entry per row, long_day on the first row, clash on the later row.
auto prep always makes a prep row (skip is the only way to have none); whole is a cut type on file.
Busy windows when the design is silent: unknown drive 60 min for moves too; no window or no start means no busy window (route_pending rows never clash).

Reply codes (reply-shapes-073.md): well formed refusals answer a code with a plain sentence and save nothing; a wrong caller raises 42501; bad content raises 22023. Day writes answer off in mode off; setup works in every mode.
proposal.md5 is the inputs_md5 of the put that made it; kept compares inputs_md5. A kept put clears the waiting proposal and sets status approved.

crew_tomorrow id = md5('hc-crew-tomorrow-v1' || market || day || approved_version || person_id)::uuid; it shares the day_before thread (day-<market>-<day>) with collapse id crew-<market>-<day>-tomorrow.
The crew_change banner is time-sensitive (aps interruption-level) only when a held reason caused it.
